purpose:
The Department for Transport is consulting on
a revised Heathrow Airport National Policy Statement (HENPS), which
would establish the policy framework against which future proposals
for airport expansion, including a potential third runway at
Heathrow Airport, would be assessed. The revised HENPS will be a
key material consideration in any future development consent
process relating to Heathrow expansion.

The Policy and Review Team, working with a broad group of officers
from across the Better Service Partnership, has prepared a detailed
response to the consultation setting out the Council's assessment
of the draft HENPS and the extent to which it addresses the likely
impacts of airport expansion on local communities. The response
highlights significant concerns regarding aircraft noise, public
health, air quality, carbon emissions, surface access, climate
change, transport infrastructure and the cumulative impacts of
further airport growth on residents.

Large parts of the borough are affected by aircraft operations and
flight paths, and residents have long experienced the impacts of
aviation noise and associated environmental effects. The Council
therefore has a direct interest in ensuring that the national
policy framework properly reflects the interests of affected
communities and places appropriate weight on environmental, health
and quality of life considerations.

The consultation response has been developed with input from
relevant service areas and reflects Wandsworth Council's
long-standing position that any proposal for airport expansion must
demonstrate that it can be delivered without unacceptable impacts
on residents, public health, the environment and the achievement of
national climate objectives.

The EYCAMHS service provides specialist mental
health support for children aged 0–5 and their families. The
service is integral to the Council’s strategic commitment to
early intervention, prevention of crisis escalation, and ensuring
children receive the right support at the right time within
community and Family Hub settings.
Performance evidence shows that the service continues to meet and
exceed expected activity levels, despite recruitment pressures, and
remains a specialist, clinically led early years mental heath offer
that is nor readily replicated in the market.
The model strongly aligns with the national Best Start in Life
strategy, which emphasises early emotional wellbeing, strong
parent-infant relationships, integrated family support and ensuring
all children achieve a good level of development by age five.
Locally, the service also supports Wandsworth’s Best Start
delivery plan and contributes to the borough-wide ambition to
strengthen early identification, improve developmental outcomes and
ensure integrated support across Family Hubs and early years
provision.
Both Children’s Services Senior Management Team (SMT) and the
Procurement Board reviewed the proposal and supported continuation
of the service through delegated award. The Board noted strong
performance, clear value for money, and evidence of effective
integration with early years and multi agency partners. No concerns
were identified regarding the provider’s quality, governance,
or ability to deliver the service.
